observations: A heavy blue line traces a large head-like shape with zigzag teeth at the bottom, scribbled oval hollows near the center, and sharp angular strokes across the top.
Soft translucent circles in lavender and pale yellow overlap across the background, forming a pastel field that sits behind the sharp blue foreground marks.
Thinner lines in gray, red, pink, and yellow thread through the interior of the blue outline, adding tangled density without overriding the dominant contour.
reading: A single heavy blue line carves out a face-like form that reads as both mask and open mouth—zigzag teeth gape, scribbled hollows stare. The soft lavender and yellow circles behind it feel almost gentle, which makes the jagged foreground more unsettling by contrast. Thin colored threads inside the outline suggest a restless interior, as though the shape is barely holding itself together.
contextAngle: As the first work in the owned Scrimshaw numbered family, this piece establishes a raw, line-driven approach. Its title neighbor Scrimshaw2 shares the teeth-and-hollow motif but fills the frame far more densely, replacing open pastel space with saturation.

connections.reason: Scrimshaw2 repeats zigzag teeth and spiral hollows but packs them into a saturated blue-green field, eliminating the open pastel breathing room seen here.
nnxyz nnotb #13 shares scribbled faces and bared teeth but builds density through layered orange and teal hatching against black, a much darker tonal range.

lookingQuestion: How does the softness of the background circles change the way you read the jagged blue teeth and scribbled hollows in the foreground?
ambiguities: Whether the blue outline describes one figure or overlapping forms is unclear; the lower section could be read as a second smaller head.
The relationship between title order and actual making sequence is not confirmed for this family.
